prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2005 manifesto (within 500 words, with ideological framing removed)

- Core objective: Withdraw the UK from the European Union by repealing the European Communities Act, restoring UK legal primacy, ending EU budget contributions, and managing a two-year transition to replace EU-derived laws and policies (agriculture, fisheries, trade, regulation).

- Trade and regulation: Maintain EU trade via bilateral agreements (as with Switzerland), regain an independent WTO seat, strengthen global trade links (Commonwealth, NAFTA, Far East). Pursue wide deregulation, especially for small businesses, including scrapping measures like the Working Time Directive where possible.

- Public finances and tax: Redirect the stated annual net EU contribution to raise state pensions by £2 per week. Temporarily increase borrowing by £3bn per year to fund immediate tax cuts and targeted spending (including defence). Immediate tax measures: halve council tax for all householders, abolish the 10% income tax band, reinstate dividend tax credits for pension funds, raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000. Longer-term: simplify taxes, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, merge National Insurance with income tax, consider a flat tax.

- Health and welfare: Decentralise NHS management; reduce targets and bureaucracy; restore stronger ward-level management; scrap Strategic Health Authorities; return hospitals to local boards; extend GP opening hours; allow more clinical discretion. Explore supplementary private insurance; remove EU limits on supplements and doctors’ hours. Simplify and reduce means-testing in benefits; caution on job programmes with limited evidence. Pensions: reinstate fund dividend tax credits; uprate frozen expatriate pensions; acknowledge need for higher saving/longer working over time.

- Education: Increase school autonomy; scrap SATs; empower heads on exclusions with alternative provision; enable specialisation and limited selection; remove central curriculum/exam interference; promote sport and trips. Expand access to private education via assisted places/vouchers/tax relief. Universities: review and defund low-standard courses; fully fund remaining; abolish top-up fees; restore maintenance grants; scrap student loans; charge EU students full fees; expand technical colleges.

- Law and order: Strengthen local accountability of police; reduce paperwork; review sentencing with credible ranges; bolster lay magistrates; reopen local courts; build prisons as needed; protect homeowners’ self-defence. Oppose EU-wide criminal procedure changes.

- Immigration and asylum: Aim for near-zero net migration via a skills-based points system applied equally to EU and non-EU applicants; tighter family routes; restore embarkation controls; language/civic tests; health checks; faster processing; stricter removals; revise domestic human-rights framework and interpret refugee rules to exclude claims via safe countries; no quotas.

- Agriculture and fisheries: Replace CAP with minimum-price/deficiency payments; cut bureaucracy; improve biosecurity at borders; reopen small abattoirs; consider restoring sector boards; support green/organic methods and diversification. Exit CFP; reassert control of UK waters; enforce conservation (licensing, mesh sizes, fallow zones).

- Defence and foreign affairs: Increase defence spending; reverse personnel/equipment cuts; retain NATO focus; withdraw from EU defence structures; prioritise UK-made kit; use independent seats in international bodies.

- Energy, environment, transport: Halt wind rollout; build new nuclear (fission) and fund fusion R&D; develop clean coal. Keep environmental policy domestic; promote recycling; restrict GM crop planting pending long-term safety evidence. Invest in roads; maintain local control of traffic policy; consider higher motorway limits and targeted speed-camera use; continue rail upgrades and allow management model changes.

- Governance and civil liberties: Preserve existing UK institutions; enable binding national referendums if 5% of the electorate petition within six months. Consider “English-only” legislative days. Scrap English regional assemblies; devolve more powers and revenues to local councils; reduce central directives. Repeal the Human Rights Act; drop ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.
